statement: Let $f(x)=(x-a)(x-b)+(x-b)(x-c)+(x-c)(x-a)$, where $a,b,c$ are real. Show that the equation $f(x)=0$ has real roots, and that these two roots are equal only when $a=b=c$.
solution: $f(x)$ is quadratic with leading coefficient $3$. Its discriminant is $4(a+b+c)^{2}-12(ab+bc+ca)=4(a^{2}+b^{2}+c^{2}-ab-bc-ca)=2\bigl((a-b)^{2}+(b-c)^{2}+(c-a)^{2}\bigr)\ge 0$, so the roots are real. The roots are equal exactly when the discriminant is zero, i.e. when $(a-b)^{2}+(b-c)^{2}+(c-a)^{2}=0$, which holds only if $a=b=c$.
hints: Compute the discriminant of the quadratic.
Rewrite the discriminant as a sum of squares.
